title: Presenilin1 inhibits glioblastoma cell invasiveness via promoting Sortilin cleavage.
authors: Yang, Wei; Xiang, Yan; Liao, Mao-Jun; Wu, Peng-Fei; Yang, Lin; Huang, Guo-Hao; Shi, Bao-Zhong; Yi, Liang; Lv, Sheng-Qing
one_liner_zh: 该文研究Presenilin1通过切割Sortilin抑制胶质母细胞瘤侵袭，属于纯细胞与肿瘤生物学研究，无蛋白质-DNA互作、无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Alzheimer's disease (AD) and glioblastoma are the most common and devastating diseases in the neurology and neurosurgery departments, respectively. Our previous research reports that the AD-related protein Presenilin1 represses cell proliferation by inhibiting the Wnt/beta-catenin pathway in glioblastoma. However, the function of Presenilin1 and the underlying mechanism need to be further investigated. METHODS: The correlations of two genes were conducted on the R2 microarray platform and CGGA. Wound healing, Transwell assays and glioblastoma transplantation were performed to detect invasion ability. Phalloidin staining was employed to show cell morphology. Proximity ligation assays and protein docking assays were employed to detect two protein locations. We also employed western blotting to detect protein expression. RESULTS: We found that Presenilin1 clearly repressed the migration, invasion and mesenchymal transition of glioblastoma cells. Intriguingly, we observed that the expression of Presenilin1 was positively correlated with Sortilin, which is identified as a pro-invasion molecule in glioma. Furthermore, Presenilin1 interacted with Sortilin at the transmembrane domain and repressed Sortilin expression by cleaving it in glioblastoma cells. First, we found that Sortilin introduced the function of Presenilin1 in phosphorylating beta-catenin and repressing invasion in glioblastoma cells. Last, Presenilin1 stimulation sharply suppressed the invasion and mesenchymal transition of glioblastoma in mouse subcutaneous and intracranial transplantation models. CONCLUSIONS: Our study reveals that Sortilin mediates the regulation of beta-catenin by Presenilin1 and transduces the anti-invasive function of Presenilin1, which may provide novel therapeutic targets for glioblastoma treatment. abstract_zh: 背景：阿尔茨海默病（Alzheimer's disease, AD）和胶质母细胞瘤分别是神经内科和神经外科最常见的破坏性疾病。我们先前的研究报道，AD相关蛋白Presenilin1通过抑制Wnt/β-catenin通路抑制胶质母细胞瘤细胞增殖。然而，Presenilin1的功能及其潜在机制仍需进一步研究。方法：在R2微阵列平台和CGGA上进行两个基因的相关性分析。采用伤口愈合实验、Transwell实验和胶质母细胞瘤移植实验检测侵袭能力。使用鬼笔环肽染色显示细胞形态。采用邻近连接实验和蛋白质对接实验检测两种蛋白的定位。我们还使用蛋白质印迹法检测蛋白表达。结果：我们发现Presenilin1明显抑制胶质母细胞瘤细胞的迁移、侵袭和间质转化。有趣的是，我们观察到Presenilin1的表达与Sortilin呈正相关，而Sortilin被鉴定为胶质瘤中的促侵袭分子。此外，Presenilin1在跨膜结构域与Sortilin相互作用，并通过切割Sortilin抑制其在胶质母细胞瘤细胞中的表达。首先，我们发现Sortilin介导了Presenilin1在胶质母细胞瘤细胞中磷酸化β-catenin和抑制侵袭的功能。最后，Presenilin1刺激在小鼠皮下和颅内移植模型中显著抑制了胶质母细胞瘤的侵袭和间质转化。结论：我们的研究揭示Sortilin介导Presenilin1对β-catenin的调控，并转导Presenilin1的抗侵袭功能，这可能为胶质母细胞瘤治疗提供新的治疗靶点。视频摘要。
